messages:
morgan: quick q — we need to tighten the SIEM export retention window. proposal: 30d for dev/test exports, 180d for infra-prod, 365d for app-prod. also need to change who can request raw exports (RBAC), and ensure exported files are wrapped with customer KMS key where applicable. thoughts?

anya: sounds fine in principle. couple things: 1) legal holds for e-discovery can override retention; 2) some infra teams rely on >180d for debugging. we should add an exception workflow.

devon: +1 on exception workflow. also: how do we plan to gate the KMS unwrap? currently export pipeline uses service-role with kms:Decrypt on the export key. we should move to an envelope pattern where the exported blob is encrypted with a per-export data key and that key is wrapped by KMS — so access checks can be done at the key-unwrap step.

eli: prev notes from incident playbook: for vuln triage we need unredacted logs for 90d by default. If we drop to 30d in dev, make sure triage runs are captured (snapshots) and attached to tickets. Otherwise we'll lose repro context.

samir: small nit: RBAC change needs a JIT access flow or an approval ticket. Otherwise too many folks will be granted long-lived read rights to SIEM exports. propose: request -> manager + sec-approver -> short-lived presigned URL (valid 24h) or a temp KMS grant.

sec-bot: automated: current export ACLs: team=infra:read, sec:read, eng-oncall:read. Lifetime: 1y. KMS key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333:key/abcd. Last rotated: 2024-11-02.

morgan: @samir that temp-KMS-grant idea is good. how would we operationalize it? do we use AWS Grant API or issue an STS token bound to a role? which is auditable?

devon: AWS Grants are not recorded in CloudTrail with granular details (pain). Better to do STS AssumeRole via a short-lived role scoped to decryption action and log AssumeRole events. Sequence: user requests -> approval service records ticket id -> approval service calls AssumeRole to generate creds -> it performs decrypt and returns pre-signed download link. All actions tied to ticket id in logs.

anya: and add a minimal RBAC change: remove org-wide "export-reader" role, replace with scoped roles per team + justification tags. We'll need a migration window and a fallback policy. Ops should get a canary group to test.

julie-legal: from legal: retention limits are fine for operational logs; for customer data we need 365d retention unless a deletion request. keep a legal_hold flag that overrides lifecycle. please document process for emergency preservation.

eli: for SIEM exports to S3, lifecycle policy snippet we can apply (example):
```json
{
  "Rules": [
    {"ID":"dev-short","Prefix":"exports/dev/","Status":"Enabled","Expiration":{"Days":30}},
    {"ID":"infra-mid","Prefix":"exports/infra/","Status":"Enabled","Expiration":{"Days":180}},
    {"ID":"prod-long","Prefix":"exports/prod/","Status":"Enabled","Expiration":{"Days":365}}
  ]
}
```

samir: we should also hash/partial-redact PII before export when possible. If that can't be guaranteed, tag the S3 object metadata as "sensitive=true" and require additional approval step.

morgan: ok action items I hear: 1) draft RBAC migration plan removing export-reader and introducing scoped roles + canary; 2) design JIT access flow (STS assume-role + ticket binding) and temp KMS decryption flow; 3) apply S3 lifecycle rules with legal_hold override; 4) update incident playbook so vuln triage has repro snapshots captured before retention expiry; 5) legal to confirm customer-data retention exceptions. i'll spin up a doc.

devon: i'll prototype the assume-role flow and put a presigned-download service behind it. will include audit annotations (ticket id, approver).

anya: i'll coordinate canary teams and draft migration timeline 30d window.

julie-legal: i'll confirm legal_hold guidance and send a template preservation request.

eli: sec-runbook update: add a checklist for exporting logs for forensic triage — include hashing step, justification, and ticket link.

morgan: thanks all. one more ask: can we get a short risk note for execs explaining tradeoffs (cost, debugging risk, compliance)? prefer a single slide.

samir: i'll draft the exec risk note with bullets and recommended mitigations.

sec-bot: automated: action created: SEC-EXPORT-2026-001 assigned to morgan, devon, anya, samir. due: 2026-04-05.
